reference_use.conclusion: The snapshot (project d8d46c95, Mathlib 25730c7c) contains the frozen Ch06 Contract; Submission is byte-identical, so child types may use only contract, SimonGMT and Mathlib names. SimonGMT supplies currents, test forms, TestFormOnConverges, simpleNVector and the weighted approximate tangent plane with uniqueness at θ(x) ≠ 0. It has no tangential gradient for Lipschitz functions on rectifiable sets, no co-area formula beyond the linear case and no slicing; Mathlib has none of these either. Those results (Simon Ch. 2, 1.5, 4.10, 6.3–6.6; Ch. 3, 1.2–1.9, 2.1–2.10; Federer 2.10.25, 3.2.22) are therefore cited inside the child proofs. Mathlib does provide: McShane (`LipschitzOnWith.extend_real`), Rademacher (`LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt`), Lebesgue differentiation (`IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average`), `ae_ball_iff`, `measurable_fderiv`, Lusin–Souslin images, `alternatizeUncurryFinCLM`/`smulRightL`/`innerSL` and second countability of C(K, F). The interior product ξ⌞(G/|G|) is written with these CLMs and evaluates by `rfl` to ξ(ν♭∧α). All seven child types elaborate in the comparator scope with the intended binder structure. The parent type is kernel-checked from five of them (axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). None of the seven names occurs in the snapshot project or among the 260 DAG nodes. The chart-cover and C¹-chart tangent lemmas of the lipschitz-pushforward branch are not yet accepted, so they cannot be reused; no accepted declaration has an identical type to any child. These checks do not certify the analytic proofs.

subproblem.title: Leibniz identity for Lipschitz multipliers on rectifiable currents (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 4.5(2), (1)–(3))
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m+1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, (M, θ, ξ) with IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ, and T ∈ D_n(U) with T(η) = ∫_M θ⟨η, ξ⟩ dHⁿ (= tauAction n M θ ξ η) for all η ∈ D^n(U). Let (μ, v) be a measure representation of T and (μ', v') one of ∂T (IsMeasureRepresentation). Let h : ℝ^P → ℝ be L_h-Lipschitz and G_h : ℝ^P → ℝ^P Borel with |G_h| ≤ L_h everywhere and the tangential-gradient property for h (for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every weighted approximate tangent plane Q of (M, θ) at x: G_h(x) ∈ Q and d/ds h(x+su)|₀ = ⟨G_h(x), u⟩ for u ∈ Q). Then for every ω ∈ D^m(U): ∫ h⟨v', ω⟩ dμ' − ∫ h⟨v, dω⟩ dμ = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(G_h(x)♭∧ω(x)) dHⁿ(x), where G_h(x)♭∧ω(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ (G_h x)).smulRight (ω x)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) (m + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), IsOpen U → IsRectifiableTriple U (m + 1) M θ ξ → (∀ η : TestFormOn U (m + 1), T η = tauAction (m + 1) M θ ξ η) → ∀ (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (v : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) (m + 1)) (μ' : Measure (Eucl P)) (v' : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) m), IsMeasureRepresentation T μ v → IsMeasureRepresentation T.boundary μ' v' → ∀ (h : Eucl P → ℝ) (Lh : ℝ≥0) (Gh : Eucl P → Eucl P), LipschitzWith Lh h → Measurable Gh → (∀ x, ‖Gh x‖ ≤ Lh) → (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Eucl P), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt (m + 1) M θ x Q → Gh x ∈ Q ∧ ∀ u ∈ Q, HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => h (x + s • u)) (inner ℝ (Gh x) u) 0) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn U m, (∫ x, h x * v' x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x) ∂μ') - (∫ x, h x * v x (exteriorDerivative (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x) ∂μ) = ∫ x in M, θ x * ξ x (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ (Gh x)).smulRight ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x))) ∂(μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl P))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P; Hᵏ := μHE[k] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure, equal to Lebesgue measure Lᵏ on ℝᵏ; H⁰ is counting measure by `euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero` and `hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton`). n := m+1. A k-covector is α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) k (continuous alternating k-form), ‖α‖ its operator norm; a k-vector is w ∈ NVector (Eucl P) k = (Covector (Eucl P) k →L[ℝ] ℝ); simple(τ) := simpleNVector τ, simple(τ)(α) = α(τ). For w ∈ ℝ^P and α ∈ Λ^k put w♭∧α := ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ w).smulRight α) ∈ Λ^{k+1}; by `alternatizeUncurryFin_apply`, (w♭∧α)(v₀,…,v_k) = Σ_{i=0}^{k} (−1)^i ⟨w, v_i⟩ α(v₀,…,v̂_i,…,v_k); it is bilinear in (w, α), ‖w♭∧α‖ ≤ (k+1)|w|‖α‖, and it equals ((alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ (Eucl P) ℝ).comp (smulRightL ℝ (Eucl P) (Covector (Eucl P) k) (innerSL ℝ w))) α by `rfl`. Fact U: if τ is orthonormal and w = ±simple(τ) then |w(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏|τ_i| = ‖α‖. Fact F (frame sign): if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of the same k-dimensional subspace, τ'_i = Σ_j B_ij τ_j with B orthogonal, then by multilinearity and alternation simple(τ') = det(B)·simple(τ) and det B = ±1. IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ means: M ⊆ U; M is Hᵏ-null-measurable; M is countably k-rectifiable; θ > 0 on M; θ is Hᵏ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U; ξ is Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable; for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M there is an orthonormal τ : Fin k → ℝ^P with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x (span τ) and ξ(x) = ±simple(τ). The weighted approximate tangent plane (Simon Ch. 3, 1.7) is unique at points where θ(x) ≠ 0 (SimonGMT `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique`); when it exists at x ∈ M we call it T_x. TG(f, G) abbreviates the tangential-gradient property: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every Q with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q, G(x) ∈ Q and for every u ∈ Q the map s ↦ f(x + s u) has derivative ⟨G(x), u⟩ at s = 0.
We follow the printed proof of Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 4.5(2), equations (1)–(3) (with the representations (2.7) of T and ∂T supplied as hypotheses). Fix ω ∈ D^m(U) and put K := tsupport ω, a compact subset of U.
1. (Preliminaries.) By IsMeasureRepresentation, x ↦ v'(x)(ω(x)) is μ'-integrable and x ↦ v(x)(dω(x)) is μ-integrable, where dω := exteriorDerivative ω ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport dω ⊆ K (`tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset`). Both integrands vanish off K (v'(x), v(x) are linear and ω, dω vanish off K), and h is bounded on K, so h·v'(ω) ∈ L¹(μ') and h·v(dω) ∈ L¹(μ). For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M (orientation clause) there is an orthonormal basis τ(x) of the weighted tangent plane T_x with ξ(x) = ±simple(τ(x)); hence |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ (Fact U).
2. (The field Y.) For x ∈ ℝ^P put Y(x) := θ(x)Σ_{i=1}^{P} ξ(x)(e_i♭∧ω(x)) e_i, so that ⟨Y(x), w⟩ = θ(x)ξ(x)(w♭∧ω(x)) for every w ∈ ℝ^P (linearity of w ↦ w♭∧ω(x)). Y is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable, vanishes off K, and |Y| ≤ (m+1)√P·θ·sup|ω| Hⁿ-a.e. on M; as θ ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K)), Y ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞M). If w ⊥ T_x then (w♭∧ω(x))(τ(x)) = Σ_i (−1)^{i−1}⟨w, τ_i(x)⟩ω(x)(…) = 0, so ⟨Y(x), w⟩ = 0; hence Y(x) ∈ T_x for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M. The right-hand side of the claim equals ∫_M ⟨Y, G_h⟩ dHⁿ (an absolutely convergent integral since |G_h| ≤ L_h).
3. (Mollification.) Let ρ_σ (σ > 0) be a standard mollifier (C^∞, ≥ 0, support in the closed σ-ball, ∫ρ_σ = 1) and h_σ := ρ_σ * h. Then h_σ is C^∞ (`HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left`), L_h-Lipschitz, |∇h_σ| ≤ L_h and |h_σ − h| ≤ L_h σ everywhere (|h_σ(x) − h(x)| ≤ ∫ρ_σ(z)|h(x−z) − h(x)| dz).
4. (Leibniz rule for h_σ; Simon's (2).) The form h_σω is C^∞ with tsupport ⊆ K, so h_σω ∈ D^m(U). By the product rule fderiv(h_σω)(x) = (Dh_σ(x)).smulRight(ω(x)) + h_σ(x)Dω(x) (`fderiv_smul`) and linearity of alternatizeUncurryFin, d(h_σω) = η_σ + h_σdω pointwise, where η_σ(x) := ∇h_σ(x)♭∧ω(x) (Dh_σ(x) = innerSL ℝ (∇h_σ(x))). Both η_σ and h_σdω are C^∞ with tsupport ⊆ K, i.e. lie in D^n(U). Hence, by linearity of T and the definition of the boundary (`GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply`), ∂T(h_σω) = T(η_σ) + T(h_σdω). By the representations, ∂T(h_σω) = ∫ v'(h_σω) dμ' = ∫ h_σ v'(ω) dμ' and T(h_σdω) = ∫ h_σ v(dω) dμ. Therefore (★) T(η_σ) = ∫ h_σ v'(ω) dμ' − ∫ h_σ v(dω) dμ.
5. (σ ↓ 0 on the right of (★).) |∫(h_σ − h)v'(ω) dμ'| ≤ L_hσ‖v'(ω)‖_{L¹(μ')} → 0 and likewise for v(dω); hence T(η_σ) → ∫ h v'(ω) dμ' − ∫ h v(dω) dμ, the left-hand side of the claim.
6. (Tau side; Simon's (3).) By hypothesis T(η_σ) = ∫_M θ ξ(η_σ) dHⁿ = ∫_M ⟨Y, ∇h_σ⟩ dHⁿ (Step 2).
7. (Weak convergence; Simon's (1).) Claim: ∫_M ⟨Y, ∇h_σ⟩ dHⁿ → ∫_M ⟨Y, G_h⟩ dHⁿ as σ ↓ 0. Charts (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 and Remark 1.3). Since M is countably n-rectifiable, M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_{j≥1} N_j with Hⁿ(N₀) = 0 and N_j embedded C¹ n-dimensional submanifolds of ℝ^P. Covering every N_j by countably many relatively compact coordinate patches we obtain countably many open Ω_j ⊆ ℝⁿ and C¹ maps Φ_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P which are Lipschitz on Ω_j and satisfy c_j|w − w'| ≤ |Φ_j(w) − Φ_j(w')| (w, w' ∈ Ω_j, some c_j > 0), with Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω_j)) = 0. Consequently Φ_j|Ω_j is injective, DΦ_j(w) is injective for w ∈ Ω_j (|DΦ_j(w)u| ≥ c_j|u|), Φ_j(Ω_j) is σ-compact hence Borel, (Φ_j|Ω_j)⁻¹ is (1/c_j)-Lipschitz hence Borel, Φ_j maps Lⁿ-null subsets of Ω_j to Hⁿ-null sets and Φ_j⁻¹ maps Hⁿ-null subsets of Φ_j(Ω_j) to Lⁿ-null sets. Put A_j(w) := DΦ_j(w) and T_j(w) := range A_j(w) (an n-dimensional subspace). Let V_j := Φ_j(Ω_j) ∖ ⋃_{i<j}Φ_i(Ω_i) (disjoint Borel). Since |⟨Y, ∇h_σ⟩| ≤ L_h|Y| ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞M) uniformly in σ and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃V_j) = 0, dominated convergence for the series over j (`tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence` or dominated convergence for ∫_M = Σ_j ∫_{M∩V_j}) reduces the claim to: for each j, ∫_{M∩V_j} ⟨Y, ∇h_σ⟩ dHⁿ → ∫_{M∩V_j} ⟨Y, G_h⟩ dHⁿ.
8. (One chart.) Fix j and write Φ, Ω, A(w) := DΦ(w), JΦ(w) := √det(A(w)ᵀA(w)) (continuous, between c_jⁿ and Lip(Φ|Ω)ⁿ on Ω). Tangent identification (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2), proof of Theorem 1.6 '⟹' and Remark 1.8(1), weighted version): if M' ⊆ U is Hᵏ-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M' and θ is Hᵏ-integrable on M' ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U, and Ψ : ℝᵏ → ℝ^P is C¹ on an open V ⊆ ℝᵏ, Lipschitz on V with a positive lower Lipschitz bound on V, then for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M' ∩ Ψ(V) the pair (M', θ) has weighted approximate tangent plane range DΨ(Ψ⁻¹x) at x. (For φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), r^{-k}∫_{M'} φ((z−x)/r)θ(z) dHᵏ(z) splits into θ(x)·r^{-k}∫_{Ψ(V)} φ((z−x)/r) dHᵏ, which tends to θ(x)∫_{range DΨ} φ dHᵏ because Ψ(V) is a C¹ k-submanifold at x; the error r^{-k}∫_{M'∩Ψ(V)} φ(·)(θ − θ(x)) dHᵏ, which tends to 0 at Lebesgue points of θ for the Radon measure Hᵏ⌞(M'∩Ψ(V)∩K); and the parts over Ψ(V) ∖ M' and M' ∖ Ψ(V), which tend to 0 at Hᵏ-a.e. point of M' ∩ Ψ(V) by the upper-density theorem, Simon Ch. 1, 3.6, since Hᵏ⌞(Ψ(V)∖M') and θHᵏ⌞(M'∖Ψ(V)) are locally finite and vanish on M' ∩ Ψ(V).) Uniqueness at θ(x) > 0 then identifies every weighted approximate tangent plane at such x with range DΨ(Ψ⁻¹x). Directional derivatives (Simon Ch. 2, 4.10). Let Φ be C¹ near w, x = Φ(w), F : ℝ^P → ℝ Lipschitz with constant C, and suppose F∘Φ is differentiable at w. Then for every u ∈ ℝⁿ, s ↦ F(x + s DΦ(w)u) has derivative D(F∘Φ)(w)u at s = 0: indeed F(x + sDΦ(w)u) − F(x) = [F(Φ(w+su)) − F(Φ(w))] + [F(x + sDΦ(w)u) − F(Φ(w+su))], the first bracket is sD(F∘Φ)(w)u + o(s), and the second is bounded by C|Φ(w) + sDΦ(w)u − Φ(w+su)| = o(s). Let E := (Φ|Ω)⁻¹(M ∩ V_j). For Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ E, with x = Φ(w): T_x = range A(w) (tangent identification with M' = M, Ψ = Φ; Φ⁻¹ maps Hⁿ-null sets to Lⁿ-null sets), Y(x) ∈ T_x, the tangential-gradient property of G_h holds at x, and h∘Φ is differentiable at w (Rademacher). Put a(w) := (A(w)ᵀA(w))⁻¹A(w)ᵀY(x), so Y(x) = A(w)a(w) and |a(w)| ≤ |Y(x)|/c_j. Then ⟨Y(x), ∇h_σ(x)⟩ = ⟨a(w), A(w)ᵀ∇h_σ(Φ(w))⟩ = ⟨a(w), ∇(h_σ∘Φ)(w)⟩ (chain rule), and ⟨Y(x), G_h(x)⟩ = Σ_i a_i(w)⟨G_h(x), ∂_iΦ(w)⟩ = Σ_i a_i(w) ∂_i(h∘Φ)(w) = ⟨a(w), ∇(h∘Φ)(w)⟩, because ∂_iΦ(w) ∈ T_x, so ⟨G_h(x), ∂_iΦ(w)⟩ = d/ds h(x + s∂_iΦ(w))|₀, which equals ∂_i(h∘Φ)(w) by the directional-derivative fact. By the area formula for the injective Lipschitz map Φ|Ω (Simon Ch. 2, 4.13; Federer 3.2.3/3.2.5), ∫_{M∩V_j} F dHⁿ = ∫_E F(Φ(w))JΦ(w) dw for F ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞(M∩V_j)). With c(w) := 1_E(w)JΦ(w)a(w), which lies in L¹(Ω; ℝⁿ) since ∫|c| ≤ c_j⁻¹∫_{M∩V_j}|Y| dHⁿ, we get ∫_{M∩V_j}⟨Y, ∇h_σ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_Ω ⟨c, ∇u_σ⟩ dw and ∫_{M∩V_j}⟨Y, G_h⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_Ω ⟨c, ∇u⟩ dw, where u_σ := h_σ∘Φ and u := h∘Φ.
9. (Weak-* convergence of gradients.) u_σ → u uniformly on Ω (|h_σ − h| ≤ L_hσ), and |∇u_σ|, |∇u| ≤ L_h·Lip(Φ|Ω) (a.e. for u). For c' ∈ C_c^1(Ω; ℝⁿ), ∫⟨c', ∇u_σ⟩ = −∫u_σ div c' → −∫u div c' = ∫⟨c', ∇u⟩: the last equality is integration by parts for the locally Lipschitz u, obtained from Fubini's theorem and the absolute continuity of u on almost every line parallel to a coordinate axis, where the partial derivatives exist a.e. and coincide with those of the Rademacher differential. For general c ∈ L¹(Ω; ℝⁿ) and δ > 0 choose c' ∈ C_c^1 with ‖c − c'‖_{L¹} < δ (density); then limsup_σ |∫⟨c, ∇u_σ⟩ − ∫⟨c, ∇u⟩| ≤ 2L_hLip(Φ|Ω)δ. Hence ∫_Ω⟨c, ∇u_σ⟩ → ∫_Ω⟨c, ∇u⟩, which with Step 8 proves the claim of Step 7.
10. (Conclusion.) By Steps 5, 6 and 7, ∫ h v'(ω) dμ' − ∫ h v(dω) dμ = lim_{σ↓0} T(η_σ) = ∫_M ⟨Y, G_h⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_M θ ξ(G_h♭∧ω) dHⁿ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Integrability of h·v'(ω), h·v(dω); unit simple ξ; the L¹ field Y with ⟨Y, w⟩ = θξ(w♭∧ω), tangent to M a.e.
Mollify h; Leibniz rule d(h_σω) = ∇h_σ♭∧ω + h_σdω and the representations give T(∇h_σ♭∧ω) = ∫h_σv'(ω)dμ' − ∫h_σv(dω)dμ.
σ ↓ 0 on the representation side by uniform convergence h_σ → h.
Weak convergence ∫_M⟨Y, ∇h_σ⟩ → ∫_M⟨Y, G_h⟩ via C¹ charts, Simon Ch. 2 4.10, the area formula and weak-* convergence of D(h_σ∘Φ) (Simon 4.5(2), (1)).

audit.reason: Compact support justifies integrability even for unbounded h. Mollification gives the correctly signed smooth identity in the supplied representations. The chartwise L¹ coefficient argument and weak-* gradient convergence justify the limiting tangent integral without assuming the child or parent conclusion.
